newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end up, downside risks persist.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end up, downside risks persist.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended higher in a shortened session on Monday as Japanese traders returned to work after an extended New Year's break.
But dealers said overall sentiment remained uncertain and downside risks persisted.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract finished 110 points higher at 19,455 after hitting a low of 19,150.
A trader with a local institution said the dollar's brief surge to 117 yen and continued bullish outlook could hurt foreign buying of Japanese stocks.

"For stocks to start picking up, the dollar/yen should stabilise. If it falls further, it's not workable for foreigners to get involved in the market," he said, adding that Japanese investors were also switching to overseas markets.
He said the 19,690-19,750 region would present a stubborn barrier, but the March Nikkei should find support from bargain hunters on the lower end of 19,000.
"But we don't have a strong base yet. I have customers buying call options rather than outright futures because they're not sure. And there are willing buyers of puts whenever it goes up," he said.
